Subject: Evan Tran — ML pairing + notebook task: scheduling and environment check

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for taking the time to interview with Redwood. We want to confirm the ML pairing session and make sure your environment is ready so the interview is focused on modeling decisions and not setup hassles.

Options (PT):
- Mon 2025-11-24 10:00–11:00 PST (preferred)
- Tue 2025-11-25 14:00–15:00 PST
- Wed 2025-11-26 08:00–09:00 PST (if you need an earlier slot)

Plan for the session (60m):
- 5m intro and quick agenda
- 35m pair-programming / notebook task (shared notebook + live discussion)
- 15m design questions + wrap / Q&A
- 5m buffer

Links & prep (attached):
- Notebook template (attached): redwood-notebook-template.ipynb
- Short prep PDF with example dataset and evaluation metric: Evan_Tran_prep_notes.pdf
- CoderPad session (we use it for the runtime): https://coderpad.io/session/6a7b9c

Interviewer lineup:
- Kimberly Park (senior ML engineer) — lead for modeling section
- Logan Wright (infra) — quick infra / reproducibility questions and environment checks

If one of the times above works, reply with the slot and your timezone. If none work, give 2–3 alternatives and we’ll try to accommodate.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Technical Recruiter | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai

Thanks — confirming I’ll take the modeling portion on Mon 11/24 at 10:00 PST. Evan, quick notes from the interviewer side:

- I’ll open the shared notebook (template attached) and we’ll work on the modeling cell that ingests a small CSV (prep notes include the sample).
- If you prefer running locally that’s fine; otherwise we can run code in CoderPad. Either way, nothing beyond standard pip packages (numpy/pandas/scikit-learn/scipy) is required.
- Please make sure your Python environment has scikit-learn >=0.24. If you can’t pip during the session, let us know and we’ll adapt the task to run in CoderPad.
- Timebox: I’ll start with a problem prompt and then pair for ~35 minutes. Feel free to ask design trade-offs out loud — we care about reasoning as much as code.

See you Monday.

—Kimberly
